articles.heading: Stop Rabies
articles.article: Boehringer Ingelheim joined forces with Pet Practitioners Association of Mumbai (PPAM), a non-profit charitable organization to combat rabies in the Greater Mumbai area, to run free vaccination camps. The initiative aligns with the Indian national goal to eliminate dog-mediated rabies by 2030 through a two-pronged approach consisting of dog vaccinations and children education. As part of the partnership in 2023, Boehringer Ingelheim donated 30,000 doses of anti-rabies vaccinations and conducted a month-long awareness drive, with the support of Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), to educate 1,000 school students about rabies prevention and the human-animal bond. These efforts are being replicated in 2024.

articles.heading: Mobile Health Van
articles.article:
Our project with Mobile Health van supports underserved communities in Mumbai, one of India’s largest and most densely populated cities. Many residents have limited access to affordable primary healthcare and may postpone treatment because of cost, distance or loss of daily wages.

Americares India Foundation is a healthcare-focused non-profit organisation with experience in delivering community-based medical services. Through this partnership, a mobile health clinic takes essential healthcare directly into underserved neighbourhoods. It provides free medical consultations, screenings, basic treatment, health education and referrals across 19 community locations, with an expected capacity of approximately 21,000 consultations annually.

Through this initiative, we aim to:
• Improve access to primary healthcare for communities with limited access to formal health services
• Enable earlier identification and management of common and chronic conditions
• Reduce the financial and travel burden associated with seeking primary care
• Strengthen health awareness, referrals and continuity of care within the community

The project utilised the entire €25,000 allocated to India under SD4G.

We will continue to monitor implementation and outcomes with Americares India Foundation and share an update by end of 31st March 2027.

articles.heading: More Green
articles.article: In line with the national strategic goals to reduce carbon emissions and reach net zero by 2050, Boehringer Ingelheim contributed to the planting of 1,000 mangrove saplings in Ras al Khor Wildlife Sanctuary in Dubai in partnership with Ministry of Climate Change and Environment and Dubai Municipality. 50 Boehringer Ingelheim employees from across IMETA came together to participate in the initiative.

articles.heading: Kalben Children Village
articles.article:
Kalben is an NGO based in Turkey with a mission to raise awareness and encourage adoption, fostering, and support of children under government protection. The NGO conducts several initiatives to bridge the gap between children under protection and the general population. Boehringer Ingelheim provided financial support to help build and establish the Kalben Children Village in the Ekinlik island in Marmara Sea. The Kalben Children Village is a summer destination for children under protection which aims to provide social support through recreational activities. 

                            The village held its soft opening in 2024 with 50 children. The official launch was in May 2025 with several volunteering activities taking place throughout the year. To date, we have engaged with over 90 children at the village, making a positive impact on their lives.

articles.heading: Kalben Volunteering
articles.article: 23 employees dedicated a remarkable 1,656 hours of volunteering, positively impacting 200 children. Beyond the numbers, these volunteering efforts provided meaningful support, guidance, and opportunities that contribute to children's wellbeing, confidence, and development. By investing time and care into their lives, our employees helped create a lasting positive impact on the children's growth, sense of belonging, and future potential.

articles.heading: Access to Healthcare
articles.article: ‘Access to Healthcare’ is an end-to-end patient support program launched by Boehringer Ingelheim, in partnership with mPharma, offering equitable healthcare access for underserved communities in Kenya. Launched in September 2022, the initiative aims to enhance disease management, provide medical treatments, and ensure patient adherence to medication for non-communicable diseases such as hypertension and type 2 diabetes. The program is set to expand across the region in the coming years.

subArticles.heading: Innovation :
subArticles.article: We have successfully completed pilot project using remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) that utilizes a camera to detect subtle changes in skin color caused by blood flow, enabling non-invasive measurement of various health parameters. This project empowered healthcare workers in remote dispensaries with a digital tool to enhance patient screening process that will be followed by diagnosis and enrollment in the program by physicians and/or HCPs. This technology can bridge the gap by enabling remote monitoring and diagnosis and improving healthcare equity.

Implemented 30 signed MoUs with different hospitals
Worked on enhancing the network of access for patients

articles.heading: Stop Rabies
articles.article: With our global expertise and rich legacy in dog vaccinations, including rabies, we have a responsibility to contribute to national rabies elimination efforts and support communities most affected by the disease. In Kenya, Boehringer Ingelheim’s efforts have led to the successful vaccination of more than 35,000 dogs and educated over 130,000 children in 2025.

articles.heading: Stop Rabies
articles.article: South Africa’s ‘Stop Rabies’ initiative has seen the vaccination of more than 19,000 dogs in 2023, logged in real-time through a Global Alliance for Rabies Control (GARC) surveillance app, with plans to vaccinate a further 20,000 dogs by the end of 2024. The door-to-door vaccinations were conducted in informal settlements around the Eastern Cape province with a goal to vaccinate 70 percent of the dog population by the end of 2025.

articles.heading: More Green
articles.article:
Boehringer Ingelheim Southern Africa in 2023 showcased its commitment to our Sustainable Development for Generations framework at Diepsloot Primary School. The team was very proud to say that the day was filled with hope, inspiration, and a sense of purpose. 
                    Over 120 employees from around the country came together to contribute towards a more sustainable future and held activities which included the opening of a water filtration drinking station, and ensuring clean drinking water for the school children in collaboration with an Ashoka social entrepreneur; Kusini Water. They also doubled the size of the existing vegetable garden, which is used to prepare meals for the children, thereby ensuring the school gets closer to a sustainable food source not reliant on funding.
                    The team also went the extra mile and extended the lifecycle of laptops and donated them to the school for administrative activities.

articles.heading: Dustbin Donation Initiative – Diepsloot Primary School
articles.article:
As part of our commitment to environmental sustainability and community upliftment, we donated dustbins to Diepsloot Primary School. The objective of this initiative is to encourage learners (we have reached 2056 students and 39 teachers) to keep their school grounds clean, take responsibility for their environment, and develop good waste management habits by disposing of litter appropriately.

A key component of the initiative is recycling. Waste collected through the dustbins can be sorted and sent for recycling, providing the school with an opportunity to generate funds from recyclable materials while contributing to environmental conservation.

Our colleagues (15 colleagues) were actively involved in the initiative and worked alongside the learners by participating in a schoolyard clean-up. Together, they collected litter and demonstrated the importance of keeping shared spaces clean. In addition, our team educated learners on proper hand hygiene by showing them how to wash their hands thoroughly after picking up rubbish, reinforcing both environmental responsibility and personal well-being.

This is a sustainable and ongoing initiative that promotes environmental awareness, cleanliness, recycling, and community involvement. By empowering learners to actively care for their surroundings, the programme helps create a cleaner, healthier school environment while instilling values that can have a lasting positive impact on their community.

We are excited to continue changing lives through sustainable development initiatives that create long-term growth and positive impact. We believe that meaningful change starts with small habits, and by encouraging responsible waste disposal and recycling, we are helping learners develop values that benefit both their community and the environment, one small habit change at a time.

articles.heading: Stop Rabies
articles.article:
Boehringer Ingelheim Egypt launched a pioneering public-private partnership with Egypt’s General Organization of Veterinary Services (GOVS). The partnership aims to eliminate dog-mediated human rabies and reinforce the company’s leading position in animal health and purpose-driven innovation.
                
                        The inauguartion event of the partnership convened senior government officials, veterinary experts and national media to announce the first of its kind collaboration, marked by the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) that set the stage for nationwide vaccination campaigns and public awareness efforts, starting in Al Ismailia.

articles.heading: Solarize Project
articles.article:
A milestone project made possible through months of hard work, coordination, and team dedication. Jana Al Ayadi, a Women’s Cooperative in Lebanon, is led by 12 active women and indirectly supports more than 50 households. The cooperative specializes in natural, preservative-free agro-food products and plays a vital role in the local economic development.

The Cooperative received a donation from Boehringer Ingelheim to facilitate the installation of a solar energy system and assist in obtaining an ISO certification. This initiative aims to enhance the Cooperative’s operational efficiency and sustainability, ensuring long-term growth and resilience.

tabs.title: Making More Health
tabs.text: To date, 800 colleagues from the IMETA region have registered on Making More Health Connect platform and every month, an average of 15 individuals are actively engaged with social entrepreneurs. In 2023, 3 colleagues from IMETA participated in Making More Health Leadership Week and 2 colleagues participated in 2024. In total, 48 IMETA employees have mentored 10 different social entrepreneurs in Boehringer Ingelheim’s incubator, accelerator and social engagement programs.
